newsitem.title: ITALY: Lira deal to hit metalworker talks - industry boss.
newsitem.headline: Lira deal to hit metalworker talks - industry boss.

text.p: The lira's return to the European currency grid at a central parity of 990 per mark will make a solution to the standoff over Italian metalworkers' contracts more difficult, the head of the employers' body said on Tuesday.

Contracts for some 1.7 million metal and engineering workers expired last June but employers and unions have failed to agree new terms. Trades unions said on Monday that they had called 10 hours of strikes to press their demands in the bitter dispute.

Gabriele Albertini, chairman of the Federmeccanica employers association, told financial daily Il Sole 24 Ore the lira's re-entry rate would have a severe effect on the competitiveness of Italian companies.

The lira returned to the ERM grid on Sunday after a four-year absence at a central rate of 990 per mark, a stronger level than Rome had wanted, following tough talks over the weekend among European Union finance ministers in Brussels.
"The impact of the new situation on contracts will be inevitable," Albertini was quoted as saying.
"The exchange rate does not help competitiveness and will force us to be rigourous over costs to the point of making a religion of it."

Monday's announcement by unions included a previously announced four-hour stoppage set for December 13 when other sectors are also due to down tools in the metalworkers' support. The other six hours would be decided at factory level.

The unions, which have previously held two eight-hour strikes on September 27 and last Friday, are protesting over a refusal by management to compensate workers in full for higher-than-expected inflation in the past contractual period.

In cash terms, unions want a gross 262,000 lire ($175) rise in their monthly pay packets, of which 97,000 is to cover the overrun in inflation between 1994 and 1996. Employers have offered 195,000 lire of which just 30,000 is for inflation.
"If we want to maintain current job levels we must be very strict on costs and therefore we can't concede one lira more with respect to inflation," Albertini told Il Sole.
"We cannot conclude inflationary contracts. We hope the unions will review their position before Thursday," he said.

Prime Minister Romano Prodi's centre-left government has said that if the employers' association, Federmeccanica, does not return to the bargaining table by November 28 it will intervene in the dispute and try to find a settlement.
